Let $(X,\mathcal A,\mu)$ and $(Y,\mathcal B,\nu)$ be sigma-finite measure
spaces, and let $f : X \times Y \to [0,\infty]$ be product-measurable. Then
$x \mapsto \int_Y f_x\,d\nu$ and $y \mapsto \int_X f^y\,d\mu$ are measurable,
and

$$\int_{X \times Y} f\,d(\mu \times \nu) = \int_X \left(\int_Y f_x\,d\nu\right)d\mu = \int_Y \left(\int_X f^y\,d\mu\right)d\nu.$$

Let $(X,\mathcal A,\mu)$ be an arbitrary measure space. All functions below have domain $X$. Let $f$ and $(f_n)$ be measurable complex-valued functions such that
$f_n\to f$ almost everywhere and $|f_n|\le g$ almost everywhere for a single
nonnegative measurable function $g$ with $\int g\,d\mu<+\infty$. Then
$f\in L^1(\mu)$,
$$\int|f_n-f|\,d\mu\longrightarrow0,$$
and hence
$$\int f_n\,d\mu\longrightarrow\int f\,d\mu.$$

derivations.claim: For almost every $y$, differentiate the product in the $z$ coordinate: $$\partial_z\bigl(z e^{-\beta H(z,y)}\bigr)=e^{-\beta H(z,y)}-\beta z\partial_zH(z,y)e^{-\beta H(z,y)}.$$ The absolute value of the right side is bounded by $(1+\beta|z\partial_zH|)e^{-\beta H}$, which is integrable by [A1].

Integrate this identity on $[-R,R]\times Y$. Absolute integrability and [F1] justify integrating first in $z$ and then in $y$, so $$\int_{[-R,R]\times Y}e^{-\beta H}\,d(z,y)-\beta\int_{[-R,R]\times Y}z\partial_zH e^{-\beta H}\,d(z,y)=\int_Y\bigl(R e^{-\beta H(R,y)}+R e^{-\beta H(-R,y)}\bigr)\,d\nu(y)=B_R.$$

The integrand in the first term is nonnegative and integrable, while the second integrand is absolutely integrable by [A1]. Their restrictions to $[-R,R]\times Y$ converge pointwise almost everywhere to the full integrands and are dominated by those integrable functions. Applying [F2] to both terms and using [A2] gives $Z-\beta\int z\partial_zH e^{-\beta H}\,d(z,y)=0$. Divide by $\beta Z>0$ to obtain the stated identity.

For finite $a<b$, integrate the same derivative over $[a,b]\times Y$. The boundary evaluation is $$\int_Y\bigl(b e^{-\beta H(b,y)}-a e^{-\beta H(a,y)}\bigr)\,d\nu(y)=Z_{[a,b]}-\beta\int_{[a,b]\times Y}z\partial_zH e^{-\beta H}\,d(z,y).$$ Dividing by $\beta Z_{[a,b]}$ and rearranging yields the displayed finite-endpoint formula.

Assume AC. Let $n\ge1$, let $O\subset\mathbb R^{2n}$ be open with its canonical symplectic form, let $H\in C^2(O,\mathbb R)$, and let $J\subset\mathbb R$ be open. Suppose $\nabla H\ne0$ on $H^{-1}(J)$ and $H^{-1}(K)$ is compact in $O$ for every compact $K\subset J$. Define $\mu_E$ by [[def-tdmath-regular-energy-shell]]. Then for every nonnegative Borel $f$ compactly supported in $H^{-1}(J)$,
$$\int_Of(x)\,dx=\int_J\mu_E(f)\,dE.$$
For every $E\in J$ with nonempty shell $\Sigma_E=H^{-1}(\{E\})$, $0<\mu_E(1)<\infty$, and $\widehat\mu_E=\mu_E/\mu_E(1)$ is a probability measure. Let $\phi_t$ be a Hamiltonian flow map defined as a diffeomorphism on a full compact energy band containing $\Sigma_E$ and preserving that band. Then $\widehat\mu_E$ is invariant under $\phi_t$ for every such regular $E$. Critical levels and noncompact bands are outside this statement.

The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> ([[def-choice-function]]).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of [[def-choice-function]]: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets ([[def-countable]]) has a choice function.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice, the exact choice strength required by
[[def-tautological-one-form-on-a-cotangent-bundle]] to construct the smooth
cotangent manifold. Let $d,N\ge1$, let $Q$ be a smooth $d$-manifold, and
choose a countable smooth-chart subcover of its atlas. Such a subcover is
obtained from a countable basis of the second-countable topology by choosing,
for each basis element contained in a chart domain, one such chart domain; this
countable selection is covered by the stated Axiom of Countable Choice. Give
$Q_N:=Q^N$ the product topology and the product smooth structure generated by
the charts
$$\left(U_1\times\cdots\times U_N,\ (q_1,\ldots,q_N)\mapsto(\phi_1(q_1),\ldots,\phi_N(q_N))\right),$$
where each $(U_i,\phi_i)$ belongs to the chosen countable subcover of charts of
$Q$. These images are open in $\mathbb R^{dN}$, and their transition maps are
componentwise smooth, so they form a smooth atlas of dimension $n=dN$; the
finite product of the countable chart family is countable. Its generated
maximal atlas is the product smooth structure in the convention of
[[def-smooth-manifold]]. The induced cotangent charts are indexed by these
base charts and form a countable atlas of $\Gamma_N$. Its
**configuration space** is $Q_N$. Its **phase space** is the cotangent bundle
$$\Gamma_N:=T^*Q_N,$$
whose points are pairs $(q,p)$ with $p\in T_q^*Q_N$. Let
$\pi_N:T^*Q_N\to Q_N$ be the cotangent-bundle projection. The **tautological
one-form** and **canonical symplectic form** are
$$\lambda_{(q,p)}(\xi):=p(d\pi_N\xi),\qquad \omega_N:=-d\lambda.$$
Thus in an induced cotangent chart $(q^1,\ldots,q^n,p_1,\ldots,p_n)$,
$$\lambda=\sum_{j=1}^n p_j\,dq^j,\qquad \omega_N=\sum_{j=1}^n dq^j\wedge dp_j.$$
The cotangent supplier proves $\omega_N$ closed and nondegenerate under the
same Countable Choice premise. On an open phase chart this is exactly the
standard form of [[def-cm-phase-domain-and-standard-symplectic-two-form]];
[[lem-cm-standard-symplectic-form-is-closed-and-nondegenerate]] gives its
closedness, contraction and nondegeneracy coordinate calculations.

Let $\mathcal F_N:=\mathcal B(\Gamma_N)$ be the Borel sigma-algebra generated
by the topology of $\Gamma_N$ ([[def-borel-sigma-algebra]]). The **Liouville
density**, denoted
$$d\Lambda_N:=|\omega_N^{\wedge n}|/n!,$$
is the positive density whose coordinate density in every induced cotangent
chart is $dq^1\cdots dq^n\,dp_1\cdots dp_n$. Define its Borel measure
$\Lambda_N$ explicitly as follows. If $\Gamma_N=\varnothing$,
set $\Lambda_N(\varnothing)=0$. Otherwise choose an at-most-countable induced
cotangent atlas $(V_k,\psi_k)_{k\in J}$ indexed by $J\subseteq\mathbb N$, order
$J$ by the usual order, and set
$$E_k:=V_k\setminus\bigcup_{j\in J,\,j<k}V_j\quad(k\in J).$$
For $A\in\mathcal F_N$, put
$$\Lambda_N(A):=\sum_{k\in J}\lambda_{2n}\bigl(\psi_k(A\cap E_k)\bigr),$$
where $\lambda_{2n}$ is Lebesgue measure on the chart image. Each $E_k$ is
Borel, and each chart map is a homeomorphism, so the terms are defined on
Borel sets. The coordinate transitions preserve $\omega_N$ because
$\omega_N=-d\lambda$ is intrinsic; hence they preserve $\omega_N^n/n!$
and have absolute Jacobian one. For two atlases, the intersections of their
disjoint chart pieces form a countable common Borel refinement. On each
nonempty refinement piece the coordinate transition is a $C^1$ diffeomorphism
with absolute Jacobian one, so the change-of-variables theorem applied to its
indicator [[thm-c-one-change-of-variables-for-nonnegative-lebesgue-measurable-functions]]
gives the same measure from either atlas. Summing over the refinement proves
atlas independence. Countable additivity follows because the chart images of
disjoint Borel sets remain disjoint within each $E_k$ and Lebesgue measure is
countably additive. For the resulting nonnegative array $a_{k\ell}$, both
$\sum_k\sum_\ell a_{k\ell}$ and $\sum_\ell\sum_k a_{k\ell}$ are the
supremum of the same finite subsums of $\{a_{k\ell}\}$, using the
nonnegative extended-sum convention of [[def-measure]]. Hence the sums
reorder and $\Lambda_N$ is a measure with the displayed coordinate density.
Given any finite constant $c_N>0$, define the **labelled reference measure**
$$m_N:=c_N\Lambda_N$$
on $(\Gamma_N,\mathcal F_N)$. It is sigma-finite: $Q_N$ is
countable-atlased as just constructed, so it is covered by countably many
cotangent chart images. Each chart image is open in $\mathbb R^{2n}$ and is
covered by the countable family of bounded open boxes with rational endpoints
whose closures lie in that chart image: every point of an open set lies in one
such box. Each box has finite Euclidean Lebesgue measure, and its chart
preimage therefore has finite $m_N$-measure because the Liouville coordinate
density is the constant $c_N$. The countably many chart-box preimages cover
$\Gamma_N$ and establish sigma-finiteness directly, without a sigma-compactness
supplier.
The constant $c_N$ is mathematical normalization data; this definition assigns
no physical unit to it.

For a partition of the particle labels into species classes of sizes
$N_1,\ldots,N_s$, let $G:=S_{N_1}\times\cdots\times S_{N_s}$ act on
$Q_N=Q^N$ by permuting factors within each class and on $T^*Q_N$ by the
cotangent lift. In canonical coordinates each lift permutes corresponding
$q$ and $p$ coordinates, so it preserves $\omega_N$, $\Lambda_N$ and $m_N$.
Let $\Pi_N:\Gamma_N\to\Gamma_N/G$ be
the orbit map, equip the orbit set with the quotient sigma-algebra
$$\mathcal F_{\mathrm{quot}}:=\{B\subseteq\Gamma_N/G:\Pi_N^{-1}(B) \text{ is Borel in }\Gamma_N\},$$
and define the **quotient reference measure** by
$$\bar m_N(B):=\frac{1}{\prod_{a=1}^s N_a!}\,m_N(\Pi_N^{-1}(B)).$$
This is a measure because inverse images preserve complements and countable
disjoint unions and $m_N$ is countably additive. The stated invariance makes
it the normalized quotient pushforward. It is a measurable quotient;
no smooth quotient structure at configurations with stabilizers is asserted.
For one species the factor is $1/N!$.

The quotient factor here is mathematical counting data. A physical postulate
determines when labels are operationally indistinguishable and how the
reference scale is interpreted; neither follows from the cotangent geometry.

$F:U\to\mathbb R^n$ be $C^1$.  Suppose $(a,b)\in U$, $F(a,b)=0$, and the

$$D_yF(a,b):\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^n,\qquad D_yF(a,b)v:=DF(a,b)(0,v),$$

$$D\varphi(x)=-D_yF(x,\varphi(x))^{-1}D_xF(x,\varphi(x)).$$

derivations.claim: In a canonical open phase domain $O\subseteq\mathbb R^{2n}$ with $m_N=c_Ndz$, hypotheses [A1]–[A2] match the published Euclidean theorem [F2]. It yields the graph-partition measure, the coarea identity, and finite positive mass on each nonempty regular level. Multiplying both the volume measure and every shell measure by the same positive constant $c_N$ preserves the identity and leaves $P_E$ unchanged.

For a compact cotangent energy band, choose finitely many canonical charts whose smaller coordinate neighborhoods cover the band and whose closures lie inside the charts. In chart coordinates, $b(s)=e^{-1/s}$ for $s>0$ and $b(s)=0$ for $s\le0$ is smooth. For a coordinate ball of squared radius $R^2$ centered at $z_0$, $b(R^2-|z-z_0|^2)$ is a smooth bump, positive on the ball and zero outside its closure. Choose finitely many such balls whose smaller concentric balls cover the band and whose closures lie inside charts. Dividing the bumps by their positive sum near the band gives a finite partition $\sum_a\chi_a=1$ on a neighborhood of the band. This uses only a finite subcover. Refine it so that one fixed $\partial_iH$ is nonzero on each chart support. By [F3], each local level is a graph $z_i=h_a(y,E)$. The map $(y,E)\mapsto(y,h_a(y,E))$ has absolute Jacobian $|\partial_Eh_a|=|\partial_iH|^{-1}$, so [F4] and [F5] give the coarea identity for $f\chi_a$. Implicit differentiation gives $\partial_yh_a=-\partial_yH/\partial_iH$, hence $$\sqrt{1+|\nabla_yh_a|^2}=|\nabla_zH|/|\partial_iH|.$$ Thus the chart term is exactly the displayed weighted area integral. Cotangent coordinate changes have block Jacobian $$\begin{pmatrix}Dq&0\\ *&Dq^{-\mathsf T}\end{pmatrix},$$ whose determinant has absolute value one; therefore the Liouville density and the chart integrals agree on overlaps. Summing the finite partition proves the coarea identity and partition independence on the cotangent band.

The shell is a closed subset of a compact inverse band, hence compact. A finite set of graph charts with $|\nabla_zH|$ bounded away from zero gives $\mu_E(1)<\infty$. A nonempty shell contains a graph patch with a nonempty open coordinate domain and positive continuous chart density, so $\mu_E(1)>0$.

Along a Hamiltonian trajectory, $\frac{d}{dt}H(\Phi_tz)=dH(X_H)(\Phi_tz)=\omega_N(X_H,X_H)=0$; therefore the flow preserves energy. The $C^2$ determinant argument in [F7] gives absolute coordinate Jacobian one for each canonical local flow. Since the reference density is $c_Ndz$, [F4] proves measure preservation on each chart; composing local flow maps retains this property. Refine the finite source and target chart covers of the compact band into disjoint Borel pieces on which each chart representation of $\Phi_t$ applies, and sum the COV identities to obtain preservation of $m_N$ on the band. By [F7]'s integral-invariance clause, the coarea identity in step 2.1 gives, for continuous compactly supported $f$ and $q\in C_c(J)$, $$\int_Jq(E)\mu_E(f\circ\Phi_t)\,dE=\int_{\Gamma_N}q(H(z))f(\Phi_tz)\,dm_N =\int_{\Gamma_N}q(H(z))f(z)\,dm_N=\int_Jq(E)\mu_E(f)\,dE.$$

On any compact subinterval of $J$, use finitely many graph charts as in step 2.1. The derivatives $|\partial_iH|$ have a positive lower bound on their compact chart supports, and the chart domains, $f$ and $\Phi_t$ are bounded there. Thus the graph integrands have one finite integrable majorant. [F6] gives continuity of both $E\mapsto\mu_E(f\circ\Phi_t)$ and $E\mapsto\mu_E(f)$ on that subinterval. Their difference integrates to zero against every compactly supported continuous $q$ by step 3.2. If it were nonzero at one energy, continuity would give a neighborhood where it has one strict sign; a nonnegative continuous bump $q$ supported there would make the integral nonzero. Hence the two shell integrals agree for every regular $E\in J$.

Fix a closed subset $F$ of a shell. In the compatible band metric from [F9], $F$ is closed and the shell is compactly contained in the band interior. Choose $\delta>0$ so the closed $\delta$-neighborhood of the shell lies in the band, and let $\eta(z)=\max(0,1-\mathrm{dist}(z,\Sigma_E)/\delta)$. It is a continuous cutoff equal to one on the shell and supported in the band. The functions $g_k(z)=\eta(z)\max(0,1-k\,\mathrm{dist}(z,F))$ converge pointwise on the shell to $\mathbf1_F$ and are bounded by one. Apply the equality proved in step 4.1 to each $g_k$, then [F6] for the finite shell measures gives equality of $\mu_E$ and its flow pushforward on every closed subset. Both measures have the same finite total mass by step 3.1; closed sets form a generating $\pi$-system. Apply [F8] and divide by $\mu_E(1)>0$ from step 3.1. Thus $P_E$ is invariant for every such regular energy.

The diagonal chart map $F$ has absolute Jacobian $\prod_j\ell_jp_{0j}=A^n$, so [F4] transforms $c_Ndq\,dp$ into $\widehat c_NdQ\,dP$. Applying the graph substitution of step 2.1 in the new coordinates gives its displayed formula with $\widetilde H$ and $\widehat c_N$; changing charts back by [F4] gives exactly the same localized shell integrals. Direct substitution in $\lambda=\sum_jp_jdq^j$ and $\omega_N=\sum_jdq^j\wedge dp_j$ proves the two pullback formulas. By the convention in [F7], contracting $X_H$ into that form gives the canonical equations $\dot q^j=\partial_{p_j}H$, $\dot p_j=-\partial_{q^j}H$. Since $\partial_{P_j}\widetilde H=p_{0j}\partial_{p_j}H$ and $\partial_{Q^j}\widetilde H=\ell_j\partial_{q^j}H$, division of the two velocity components by $\ell_j$ and $p_{0j}$ proves the stated $A^{-1}$ factors in the unchanged parameter $t$.

Let $(X,\mathcal A,\mu)$ be an arbitrary measure space. All functions below have domain $X$. Let $f$ and $(f_n)$ be measurable complex-valued functions such that
$f_n\to f$ almost everywhere and $|f_n|\le g$ almost everywhere for a single
nonnegative measurable function $g$ with $\int g\,d\mu<+\infty$. Then
$f\in L^1(\mu)$,
$$\int|f_n-f|\,d\mu\longrightarrow0,$$
and hence
$$\int f_n\,d\mu\longrightarrow\int f\,d\mu.$$

For $x\in\mathbb R$, define
$$\exp(x):=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}\frac{x^n}{\iota(n!)}, \qquad e:=\exp(1),$$
provided by the all-real convergence proved in [[lem-exponential-series-has-infinite-radius]]. Here $n!\in\mathbb N$ is the factorial of [[def-factorial-and-falling-factorial]], $\iota(n!)$ is its nonzero real image ([[def-canonical-natural]], [[lem-of-naturals-positive]]), and powers and series are those of [[def-integer-power]] and [[def-series]].

This is a real power series centred at $0$ ([[def-real-power-series-and-radius-of-convergence]]). No logarithm, irrational power, or differential equation enters the definition.

The real exponential function is $C^\infty$, and for every $m\in\mathbb N$,
$$\exp^{(m)}=\exp.$$
In particular $(\exp)'=\exp$.

Let $f:U\to V\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be totally differentiable at $a\in U$ and let $g:V\to\mathbb R^p$ be totally differentiable at $f(a)$. Then $g\circ f$ is totally differentiable at $a$ and

$$D(g\circ f)(a)=Dg(f(a))\circ Df(a).$$

Let $a, b \in \mathbb{R}$ with $a < b$ and let $f : [a,b] \to \mathbb{R}$ be
continuous on $[a,b]$ ([[def-continuity-real]], [[def-interval]]) and
differentiable at every point of $(a,b)$ as a function on $[a,b]$
([[def-derivative]]). Then there is $c \in (a,b)$ with

$$f(b) - f(a) \;=\; f'(c)\,(b - a) .$$

Equivalently, since $b - a \ne 0$, there is $c \in (a,b)$ at which
$f'(c) = \bigl(f(b)-f(a)\bigr)/(b-a)$: the derivative somewhere inside equals
the average rate of change across the whole interval.

**Continuity on the closed interval cannot be dropped.** Differentiability at
every point of $(a,b)$ alone does not suffice: a function on $[0,1]$,
differentiable at every point of $(0,1)$ with derivative constantly $1$, for
which no $c$ works, is exhibited later on this page as a false statement, and
the companion page works the same witness out in full.

For every real $x$, $\exp(x)>0$ and
$$\exp(-x)=\frac1{\exp(x)}.$$

For $x>0$, define $\log x$ to be the unique real $y$ such that $\exp(y)=x$. This is well-defined because [[cor-exponential-is-a-bijection-onto-positive-reals]] states that $\exp:\mathbb R\to(0,\infty)$ is a bijection.

Thus $\log:(0,\infty)\to\mathbb R$ is the inverse function of $\exp$. In particular, $\log(\exp y)=y$ for every $y\in\mathbb R$ and $\exp(\log x)=x$ for every $x>0$.

For $x>0$, $\log$ is differentiable and
$$\log'(x)=\frac1x,\qquad \log x=\int_1^x\frac{dt}{t}.$$

Let $(\Gamma_N,\mathcal F_N,m_N)$ be a sigma-finite phase-reference measure
space from [[def-csm-phase-space-reference]]; the cotangent construction uses
the stated Axiom of Countable Choice
([[def-countable-choice]]). A **statistical state** is a probability measure
$P$ on $(\Gamma_N,\mathcal F_N)$, meaning a countably additive measure with
$P(\Gamma_N)=1$ ([[def-measure]]). A **density** of $P$ relative to $m_N$ is a
measurable $\rho:\Gamma_N\to[0,\infty]$ such that
$$P(A)=\int_A\rho\,dm_N\quad(A\in\mathcal F_N),\qquad \int_{\Gamma_N}\rho\,dm_N=1.$$
Equivalently, $P=\rho\,m_N$ in the definition of a measure with density
([[def-measure-with-density]]); integration against that density has the
meaning supplied by [[thm-integration-against-a-density]]. A state need not
have a density.

An **observable** is a real-valued measurable function
$A:\Gamma_N\to\mathbb R$ ([[def-extended-real-valued-measurable-function]]).
Its expectation $\langle A\rangle_P:=\int A\,dP$ is used only when $A$ is
integrable, that is, $\int|A|\,dP<\infty$
([[def-integrable-real-and-complex-functions-and-their-integrals]]). Its
variance is
$$\operatorname{Var}_P(A):=\int(A-\langle A\rangle_P)^2\,dP$$
when $A^2$ is integrable. For square-integrable $A,B$, their covariance is
$$\operatorname{Cov}_P(A,B):=\int(A-\langle A\rangle_P)(B-\langle B\rangle_P)\,dP.$$
These expressions are finite under the stated square-integrability
hypotheses. Indeed, $P(\Gamma_N)=1$ makes $1\in L^2(P)$ with norm $1$.
By [[cor-cauchy-schwarz-inequality-for-l-two]],
$\int|A|\,dP\le(\int A^2\,dP)^{1/2}$, so the mean of a square-integrable
observable exists. If $a=\langle A\rangle_P$, then
$|A-a|^2\le2A^2+2a^2$ makes $A-a$ square-integrable; the same argument
applies to $B-b$. A second application of that inequality gives
$\int|(A-a)(B-b)|\,dP\le\|A-a\|_2\|B-b\|_2<\infty$.
Thus both the variance and covariance integrals above are well-defined.

If $P=\rho m_N$ and the integrals are defined, these expectations equal
$\int A\rho\,dm_N$ by [[thm-integration-against-a-density]].

A **macrostate map** is a measurable map
$M:(\Gamma_N,\mathcal F_N)\to(Y,\mathcal G)$. Its induced state on $Y$ is
the pushforward $M_*P(B):=P(M^{-1}(B))$. The measure of a macrocell and an
entropy assigned to that macrostate are additional constructions; they are
not identical to the expectation or variance of a microscopic observable.

derivations.claim: For each fixed $\theta\in\Theta$, choose a compact neighborhood $K$ of $\theta$. The bound in [A1] implies $\int we^{\theta\cdot X}dm<\infty$. On $\{w>0\}$ the integrand is strictly positive by [F3]; since this set is the countable union of the sets $\{we^{\theta\cdot X}\ge1/k\}$, at least one has positive measure. Hence $Z(\theta)>0$ as well as finite.

For coordinate $a$, choose a compact neighborhood $K$ of $\theta$ containing every $\theta+se_a$ with $|s|\le\epsilon$. The mean-value theorem and chain rule [F2] bound the difference quotient by $w|X_a|\sup_{|s|\le\epsilon}e^{(\theta+se_a)\cdot X}$. Since $|X_a|\le1+\sum_c|X_c|^2$, [A1] bounds this entire supremum pointwise by the single integrable $G_K$. Thus [F1] gives $\partial_aZ=\int wX_ae^{\theta\cdot X}dm$. Applying the same argument to the first derivative, with $|X_aX_b|\le(|X_a|^2+|X_b|^2)/2$, gives $\partial_b\partial_aZ=\int wX_aX_be^{\theta\cdot X}dm$. The same local envelopes and [F1] give continuity of these derivatives, hence $Z\in C^2$.

By [F3], dividing the first-derivative formula by $Z>0$ gives $\partial_a\log Z=\langle X_a\rangle_\theta$. Differentiating once more yields $$\partial_b\partial_a\log Z=\frac{\int X_aX_bwe^{\theta\cdot X}dm}{Z} -\frac{\int X_awe^{\theta\cdot X}dm\int X_bwe^{\theta\cdot X}dm}{Z^2} =\langle X_aX_b\rangle-\langle X_a\rangle\langle X_b\rangle.$$ This is the covariance in [F4]. Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $\Gamma_N=T^*Q_N$ be a cotangent phase space
from [[def-csm-phase-space-reference]], with $\dim Q_N=n$, and let $J\subseteq
\mathbb R$ be open. Let $H:\Gamma_N\to\mathbb R$ have a $C^2$ coordinate
representative $H\circ\psi^{-1}$ in every canonical cotangent chart $\psi$;
write $dH$ for the resulting differential. Assume
$dH\ne0$ on $H^{-1}(J)$ and suppose $H^{-1}(K)$ is compact for every compact
$K\subset J$. Use the real canonical cotangent coordinates
$z=(q^1,\ldots,q^n,p_1,\ldots,p_n)$ of
[[def-csm-phase-space-reference]]; this mathematical theorem assigns no
physical units to these coordinates.

For a compact regular energy band, take a finite smooth partition of unity
$\{\chi_a\}$ subordinate to canonical cotangent charts. In a chart where
$\partial_iH\ne0$, write the local energy graph as $z_i=h_a(y,E)$ and define
the **weighted shell measure** on nonnegative Borel $f$ by
$$\mu_E(f):=c_N\sum_a\int f(y,h_a(y,E))\chi_a(y,h_a(y,E))|\partial_iH(y,h_a(y,E))|^{-1}\,dy,$$
where $c_N>0$ is the constant density of the reference measure in canonical
coordinates. Then this definition is independent of the chosen finite chart
partition and equals the chart expression
$$\mu_E(f)=c_N\int_{\Sigma_E}f(z)|\nabla_zH(z)|^{-1}\,dA_z,$$
with $\Sigma_E:=H^{-1}(\{E\})$ and Euclidean area in each real
canonical chart. For every nonnegative Borel $f$ compactly supported in
$H^{-1}(J)$,
$$\int_{\Gamma_N}f\,dm_N=\int_J\mu_E(f)\,dE.$$
If $\Sigma_E$ is nonempty, then $0<\mu_E(1)<\infty$ and
$P_E:=\mu_E/\mu_E(1)$ is a probability measure. If a Hamiltonian flow map is a
$C^1$ diffeomorphism on a full compact energy band and preserves that band,
then $P_E$ is invariant under that map for every such regular $E$. Critical
levels and noncompact inverse bands are outside this statement. For its
invariance clause, fix a compatible metric on a compact band whose interior
contains the shell; such a metric exists by
[[thm-topological-manifolds-are-metrizable-and-paracompact]].

The same shell measure can be computed after a fixed numerical coordinate
normalization. Choose positive real scales $\ell_j,p_{0j}$ with a common
product $\ell_jp_{0j}=A>0$, and put
$$q^j=\ell_jQ^j,\qquad p_j=p_{0j}P_j,\qquad F(Q,P)=(q,p),\qquad \widetilde H=H\circ F.$$
The reference density becomes $\widehat c_N\,dQ\,dP$ with
$\widehat c_N=c_NA^n$. The graph and weighted-area formulas above then use
$\widetilde H$, its gradient and Euclidean area in $(Q,P)$, and
$\widehat c_N$, with the same energy variable $E$. They describe the
pullback of $\mu_E$, not a different shell law. The pulled-back forms are
$$F^*\lambda=A\sum_jP_j\,dQ^j,\qquad F^*\omega_N=A\sum_jdQ^j\wedge dP_j.$$
For a Hamiltonian trajectory parameterized by its original $t$, the equations
in these coordinates are
$$\frac{dQ^j}{dt}=A^{-1}\partial_{P_j}\widetilde H,\qquad \frac{dP_j}{dt}=-A^{-1}\partial_{Q^j}\widetilde H.$$
This chart normalization does not rescale $H$, $E$ or $t$.

The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> ([[def-choice-function]]).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice, the exact choice strength required by
[[def-tautological-one-form-on-a-cotangent-bundle]] to construct the smooth
cotangent manifold. Let $d,N\ge1$, let $Q$ be a smooth $d$-manifold, and
choose a countable smooth-chart subcover of its atlas. Such a subcover is
obtained from a countable basis of the second-countable topology by choosing,
for each basis element contained in a chart domain, one such chart domain; this
countable selection is covered by the stated Axiom of Countable Choice. Give
$Q_N:=Q^N$ the product topology and the product smooth structure generated by
the charts
$$\left(U_1\times\cdots\times U_N,\ (q_1,\ldots,q_N)\mapsto(\phi_1(q_1),\ldots,\phi_N(q_N))\right),$$
where each $(U_i,\phi_i)$ belongs to the chosen countable subcover of charts of
$Q$. These images are open in $\mathbb R^{dN}$, and their transition maps are
componentwise smooth, so they form a smooth atlas of dimension $n=dN$; the
finite product of the countable chart family is countable. Its generated
maximal atlas is the product smooth structure in the convention of
[[def-smooth-manifold]]. The induced cotangent charts are indexed by these
base charts and form a countable atlas of $\Gamma_N$. Its
**configuration space** is $Q_N$. Its **phase space** is the cotangent bundle
$$\Gamma_N:=T^*Q_N,$$
whose points are pairs $(q,p)$ with $p\in T_q^*Q_N$. Let
$\pi_N:T^*Q_N\to Q_N$ be the cotangent-bundle projection. The **tautological
one-form** and **canonical symplectic form** are
$$\lambda_{(q,p)}(\xi):=p(d\pi_N\xi),\qquad \omega_N:=-d\lambda.$$
Thus in an induced cotangent chart $(q^1,\ldots,q^n,p_1,\ldots,p_n)$,
$$\lambda=\sum_{j=1}^n p_j\,dq^j,\qquad \omega_N=\sum_{j=1}^n dq^j\wedge dp_j.$$
The cotangent supplier proves $\omega_N$ closed and nondegenerate under the
same Countable Choice premise. On an open phase chart this is exactly the
standard form of [[def-cm-phase-domain-and-standard-symplectic-two-form]];
[[lem-cm-standard-symplectic-form-is-closed-and-nondegenerate]] gives its
closedness, contraction and nondegeneracy coordinate calculations.

Let $\mathcal F_N:=\mathcal B(\Gamma_N)$ be the Borel sigma-algebra generated
by the topology of $\Gamma_N$ ([[def-borel-sigma-algebra]]). The **Liouville
density**, denoted
$$d\Lambda_N:=|\omega_N^{\wedge n}|/n!,$$
is the positive density whose coordinate density in every induced cotangent
chart is $dq^1\cdots dq^n\,dp_1\cdots dp_n$. Define its Borel measure
$\Lambda_N$ explicitly as follows. If $\Gamma_N=\varnothing$,
set $\Lambda_N(\varnothing)=0$. Otherwise choose an at-most-countable induced
cotangent atlas $(V_k,\psi_k)_{k\in J}$ indexed by $J\subseteq\mathbb N$, order
$J$ by the usual order, and set
$$E_k:=V_k\setminus\bigcup_{j\in J,\,j<k}V_j\quad(k\in J).$$
For $A\in\mathcal F_N$, put
$$\Lambda_N(A):=\sum_{k\in J}\lambda_{2n}\bigl(\psi_k(A\cap E_k)\bigr),$$
where $\lambda_{2n}$ is Lebesgue measure on the chart image. Each $E_k$ is
Borel, and each chart map is a homeomorphism, so the terms are defined on
Borel sets. The coordinate transitions preserve $\omega_N$ because
$\omega_N=-d\lambda$ is intrinsic; hence they preserve $\omega_N^n/n!$
and have absolute Jacobian one. For two atlases, the intersections of their
disjoint chart pieces form a countable common Borel refinement. On each
nonempty refinement piece the coordinate transition is a $C^1$ diffeomorphism
with absolute Jacobian one, so the change-of-variables theorem applied to its
indicator [[thm-c-one-change-of-variables-for-nonnegative-lebesgue-measurable-functions]]
gives the same measure from either atlas. Summing over the refinement proves
atlas independence. Countable additivity follows because the chart images of
disjoint Borel sets remain disjoint within each $E_k$ and Lebesgue measure is
countably additive. For the resulting nonnegative array $a_{k\ell}$, both
$\sum_k\sum_\ell a_{k\ell}$ and $\sum_\ell\sum_k a_{k\ell}$ are the
supremum of the same finite subsums of $\{a_{k\ell}\}$, using the
nonnegative extended-sum convention of [[def-measure]]. Hence the sums
reorder and $\Lambda_N$ is a measure with the displayed coordinate density.
Given any finite constant $c_N>0$, define the **labelled reference measure**
$$m_N:=c_N\Lambda_N$$
on $(\Gamma_N,\mathcal F_N)$. It is sigma-finite: $Q_N$ is
countable-atlased as just constructed, so it is covered by countably many
cotangent chart images. Each chart image is open in $\mathbb R^{2n}$ and is
covered by the countable family of bounded open boxes with rational endpoints
whose closures lie in that chart image: every point of an open set lies in one
such box. Each box has finite Euclidean Lebesgue measure, and its chart
preimage therefore has finite $m_N$-measure because the Liouville coordinate
density is the constant $c_N$. The countably many chart-box preimages cover
$\Gamma_N$ and establish sigma-finiteness directly, without a sigma-compactness
supplier.
The constant $c_N$ is mathematical normalization data; this definition assigns
no physical unit to it.

cotangent manifold. Let $d,N\ge1$, let $Q$ be a smooth $d$-manifold, and
choose a countable smooth-chart subcover of its atlas. Such a subcover is
obtained from a countable basis of the second-countable topology by choosing,
for each basis element contained in a chart domain, one such chart domain; this
countable selection is covered by the stated Axiom of Countable Choice. Give
$Q_N:=Q^N$ the product topology and the product smooth structure generated by
the charts
$$\left(U_1\times\cdots\times U_N,\ (q_1,\ldots,q_N)\mapsto(\phi_1(q_1),\ldots,\phi_N(q_N))\right),$$
where each $(U_i,\phi_i)$ belongs to the chosen countable subcover of charts of
$Q$. These images are open in $\mathbb R^{dN}$, and their transition maps are
componentwise smooth, so they form a smooth atlas of dimension $n=dN$; the
finite product of the countable chart family is countable. Its generated
maximal atlas is the product smooth structure in the convention of
[[def-smooth-manifold]]. The induced cotangent charts are indexed by these
base charts and form a countable atlas of $\Gamma_N$. Its
**configuration space** is $Q_N$. Its **phase space** is the cotangent bundle
$$\Gamma_N:=T^*Q_N,$$
whose points are pairs $(q,p)$ with $p\in T_q^*Q_N$. Let
$\pi_N:T^*Q_N\to Q_N$ be the cotangent-bundle projection. The **tautological
one-form** and **canonical symplectic form** are
$$\lambda_{(q,p)}(\xi):=p(d\pi_N\xi),\qquad \omega_N:=-d\lambda.$$
Thus in an induced cotangent chart $(q^1,\ldots,q^n,p_1,\ldots,p_n)$,
$$\lambda=\sum_{j=1}^n p_j\,dq^j,\qquad \omega_N=\sum_{j=1}^n dq^j\wedge dp_j.$$
The cotangent supplier proves $\omega_N$ closed and nondegenerate under the
same Countable Choice premise. On an open phase chart this is exactly the
standard form of [[def-cm-phase-domain-and-standard-symplectic-two-form]];
[[lem-cm-standard-symplectic-form-is-closed-and-nondegenerate]] gives its
closedness, contraction and nondegeneracy coordinate calculations.

Let $\mathcal F_N:=\mathcal B(\Gamma_N)$ be the Borel sigma-algebra generated
by the topology of $\Gamma_N$ ([[def-borel-sigma-algebra]]). The **Liouville
density**, denoted
$$d\Lambda_N:=|\omega_N^{\wedge n}|/n!,$$
is the positive density whose coordinate density in every induced cotangent
chart is $dq^1\cdots dq^n\,dp_1\cdots dp_n$. Define its Borel measure
$\Lambda_N$ explicitly as follows. If $\Gamma_N=\varnothing$,
set $\Lambda_N(\varnothing)=0$. Otherwise choose an at-most-countable induced
cotangent atlas $(V_k,\psi_k)_{k\in J}$ indexed by $J\subseteq\mathbb N$, order
$J$ by the usual order, and set
$$E_k:=V_k\setminus\bigcup_{j\in J,\,j<k}V_j\quad(k\in J).$$
For $A\in\mathcal F_N$, put
$$\Lambda_N(A):=\sum_{k\in J}\lambda_{2n}\bigl(\psi_k(A\cap E_k)\bigr),$$
where $\lambda_{2n}$ is Lebesgue measure on the chart image. Each $E_k$ is
Borel, and each chart map is a homeomorphism, so the terms are defined on
Borel sets. The coordinate transitions preserve $\omega_N$ because
$\omega_N=-d\lambda$ is intrinsic; hence they preserve $\omega_N^n/n!$
and have absolute Jacobian one. For two atlases, the intersections of their
disjoint chart pieces form a countable common Borel refinement. On each
nonempty refinement piece the coordinate transition is a $C^1$ diffeomorphism
with absolute Jacobian one, so the change-of-variables theorem applied to its
indicator [[thm-c-one-change-of-variables-for-nonnegative-lebesgue-measurable-functions]]
gives the same measure from either atlas. Summing over the refinement proves
atlas independence. Countable additivity follows because the chart images of
disjoint Borel sets remain disjoint within each $E_k$ and Lebesgue measure is
countably additive. For the resulting nonnegative array $a_{k\ell}$, both
$\sum_k\sum_\ell a_{k\ell}$ and $\sum_\ell\sum_k a_{k\ell}$ are the
supremum of the same finite subsums of $\{a_{k\ell}\}$, using the
nonnegative extended-sum convention of [[def-measure]]. Hence the sums
reorder and $\Lambda_N$ is a measure with the displayed coordinate density.
Given any finite constant $c_N>0$, define the **labelled reference measure**
$$m_N:=c_N\Lambda_N$$
on $(\Gamma_N,\mathcal F_N)$. It is sigma-finite: $Q_N$ is
countable-atlased as just constructed, so it is covered by countably many
cotangent chart images. Each chart image is open in $\mathbb R^{2n}$ and is
covered by the countable family of bounded open boxes with rational endpoints
whose closures lie in that chart image: every point of an open set lies in one
such box. Each box has finite Euclidean Lebesgue measure, and its chart
preimage therefore has finite $m_N$-measure because the Liouville coordinate
density is the constant $c_N$. The countably many chart-box preimages cover
$\Gamma_N$ and establish sigma-finiteness directly, without a sigma-compactness
supplier.
The constant $c_N$ is mathematical normalization data; this definition assigns
no physical unit to it.

For a partition of the particle labels into species classes of sizes
$N_1,\ldots,N_s$, let $G:=S_{N_1}\times\cdots\times S_{N_s}$ act on
$Q_N=Q^N$ by permuting factors within each class and on $T^*Q_N$ by the
cotangent lift. In canonical coordinates each lift permutes corresponding
$q$ and $p$ coordinates, so it preserves $\omega_N$, $\Lambda_N$ and $m_N$.
Let $\Pi_N:\Gamma_N\to\Gamma_N/G$ be
the orbit map, equip the orbit set with the quotient sigma-algebra
$$\mathcal F_{\mathrm{quot}}:=\{B\subseteq\Gamma_N/G:\Pi_N^{-1}(B) \text{ is Borel in }\Gamma_N\},$$
and define the **quotient reference measure** by
$$\bar m_N(B):=\frac{1}{\prod_{a=1}^s N_a!}\,m_N(\Pi_N^{-1}(B)).$$
This is a measure because inverse images preserve complements and countable
disjoint unions and $m_N$ is countably additive. The stated invariance makes
it the normalized quotient pushforward. It is a measurable quotient;
no smooth quotient structure at configurations with stabilizers is asserted.
For one species the factor is $1/N!$.

The quotient factor here is mathematical counting data. A physical postulate
determines when labels are operationally indistinguishable and how the
reference scale is interpreted; neither follows from the cotangent geometry.

On a $2n$-dimensional symplectic manifold, every Hamiltonian local flow
preserves the Liouville volume form $\Omega=\omega^n/n!$.

If $T$ preserves $\mu$ and $f:X\to[0,\infty]$ is measurable, then $\int f\circ T\,d\mu=\int f\,d\mu$, allowing infinity. If $f$ is integrable real or complex valued, $f\circ T$ is integrable and the same equality holds. Conversely, for a measurable self-map, equality for every measurable indicator implies measure preservation.

$U,V \subseteq \mathbb R^n$ be open and let $T : U \to V$ be a
$C^1$ diffeomorphism. For every nonnegative Lebesgue measurable
$f : V \to [0,\infty]$,
$$ \int_V f(y)\,d\lambda_n(y) = \int_U f(T(x))\,|\det DT(x)|\,d\lambda_n(x). $$

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of [[def-choice-function]]: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets ([[def-countable]]) has a choice function.

Let $(\Gamma_N,\mathcal F_N,m_N)$ be a sigma-finite phase-reference measure
space from [[def-csm-phase-space-reference]]; the cotangent construction uses
the stated Axiom of Countable Choice
([[def-countable-choice]]). A **statistical state** is a probability measure
$P$ on $(\Gamma_N,\mathcal F_N)$, meaning a countably additive measure with
$P(\Gamma_N)=1$ ([[def-measure]]). A **density** of $P$ relative to $m_N$ is a
measurable $\rho:\Gamma_N\to[0,\infty]$ such that
$$P(A)=\int_A\rho\,dm_N\quad(A\in\mathcal F_N),\qquad \int_{\Gamma_N}\rho\,dm_N=1.$$
Equivalently, $P=\rho\,m_N$ in the definition of a measure with density
([[def-measure-with-density]]); integration against that density has the
meaning supplied by [[thm-integration-against-a-density]]. A state need not
have a density.

An **observable** is a real-valued measurable function
$A:\Gamma_N\to\mathbb R$ ([[def-extended-real-valued-measurable-function]]).
Its expectation $\langle A\rangle_P:=\int A\,dP$ is used only when $A$ is
integrable, that is, $\int|A|\,dP<\infty$
([[def-integrable-real-and-complex-functions-and-their-integrals]]). Its
variance is
$$\operatorname{Var}_P(A):=\int(A-\langle A\rangle_P)^2\,dP$$
when $A^2$ is integrable. For square-integrable $A,B$, their covariance is
$$\operatorname{Cov}_P(A,B):=\int(A-\langle A\rangle_P)(B-\langle B\rangle_P)\,dP.$$
These expressions are finite under the stated square-integrability
hypotheses. Indeed, $P(\Gamma_N)=1$ makes $1\in L^2(P)$ with norm $1$.
By [[cor-cauchy-schwarz-inequality-for-l-two]],
$\int|A|\,dP\le(\int A^2\,dP)^{1/2}$, so the mean of a square-integrable
observable exists. If $a=\langle A\rangle_P$, then
$|A-a|^2\le2A^2+2a^2$ makes $A-a$ square-integrable; the same argument
applies to $B-b$. A second application of that inequality gives
$\int|(A-a)(B-b)|\,dP\le\|A-a\|_2\|B-b\|_2<\infty$.
Thus both the variance and covariance integrals above are well-defined.

If $P=\rho m_N$ and the integrals are defined, these expectations equal
$\int A\rho\,dm_N$ by [[thm-integration-against-a-density]].

A **macrostate map** is a measurable map
$M:(\Gamma_N,\mathcal F_N)\to(Y,\mathcal G)$. Its induced state on $Y$ is
the pushforward $M_*P(B):=P(M^{-1}(B))$. The measure of a macrocell and an
entropy assigned to that macrostate are additional constructions; they are
not identical to the expectation or variance of a microscopic observable.

obtained from a countable basis of the second-countable topology by choosing,

countable selection is covered by the stated Axiom of Countable Choice. Give

$$\left(U_1\times\cdots\times U_N,\ (q_1,\ldots,q_N)\mapsto(\phi_1(q_1),\ldots,\phi_N(q_N))\right),$$

componentwise smooth, so they form a smooth atlas of dimension $n=dN$; the

maximal atlas is the product smooth structure in the convention of
[[def-smooth-manifold]]. The induced cotangent charts are indexed by these
base charts and form a countable atlas of $\Gamma_N$. Its
**configuration space** is $Q_N$. Its **phase space** is the cotangent bundle

standard form of [[def-cm-phase-domain-and-standard-symplectic-two-form]];

set $\Lambda_N(\varnothing)=0$. Otherwise choose an at-most-countable induced
cotangent atlas $(V_k,\psi_k)_{k\in J}$ indexed by $J\subseteq\mathbb N$, order

Borel sets. The coordinate transitions preserve $\omega_N$ because

and have absolute Jacobian one. For two atlases, the intersections of their
disjoint chart pieces form a countable common Borel refinement. On each
nonempty refinement piece the coordinate transition is a $C^1$ diffeomorphism

indicator [[thm-c-one-change-of-variables-for-nonnegative-lebesgue-measurable-functions]]

supremum of the same finite subsums of $\{a_{k\ell}\}$, using the
nonnegative extended-sum convention of [[def-measure]]. Hence the sums
reorder and $\Lambda_N$ is a measure with the displayed coordinate density.

$$m_N:=c_N\Lambda_N$$
on $(\Gamma_N,\mathcal F_N)$. It is sigma-finite: $Q_N$ is
countable-atlased as just constructed, so it is covered by countably many
cotangent chart images. Each chart image is open in $\mathbb R^{2n}$ and is
covered by the countable family of bounded open boxes with rational endpoints
whose closures lie in that chart image: every point of an open set lies in one
such box. Each box has finite Euclidean Lebesgue measure, and its chart
preimage therefore has finite $m_N$-measure because the Liouville coordinate
density is the constant $c_N$. The countably many chart-box preimages cover
$\Gamma_N$ and establish sigma-finiteness directly, without a sigma-compactness
supplier.

**(a) Dimensions.** Write $\ell$, $\tau$, $\mu$ for the three independent *dimension symbols* of length, duration and mass. A **dimension** is an element of the free abelian group generated by $\ell,\tau,\mu$, that is, a triple $(a,b,c)\in\mathbb Z^3$ written $\ell^{a}\tau^{b}\mu^{c}$; **products and inverses** of dimensions are componentwise addition and negation, so that $\ell^{a}\tau^{b}\mu^{c}\cdot\ell^{a'}\tau^{b'}\mu^{c'}=\ell^{a+a'}\tau^{b+b'}\mu^{c+c'}$ and $(\ell^{a}\tau^{b}\mu^{c})^{-1}=\ell^{-a}\tau^{-b}\mu^{-c}$. The **dimensionless** dimension is $\ell^{0}\tau^{0}\mu^{0}$, abbreviated $1$.

**(b) The dimension map.** The conventions assign to the quantities of the framework a **dimension** $[X]$, subject to the rules

$$[XY]=[X][Y],\qquad [X/Y]=[X][Y]^{-1},\qquad \left[\frac{dX}{du}\right]=[X][u]^{-1},$$

and to the requirement that a sum $X+Y$ is meaningful only when $[X]=[Y]$, in which case $[X+Y]=[X]$. The third rule applies to a differentiable dependence of a quantity $X$ on a quantity $u$ and covers iterated differentiation, so that $[d^{2}X/du^{2}]=[X][u]^{-2}$. The assignment is part of the conventions: the rules above are consistency requirements on it, not physical laws and not theorems.

**(c) Reference units.** The **metre** is the reference unit of length, the **second** the reference unit of duration and the **kilogram** the reference unit of mass. A quantity of dimension $\ell^{a}\tau^{b}\mu^{c}$ is expressed in the unit $\mathrm m^{a}\,\mathrm s^{b}\,\mathrm{kg}^{c}$: its value is a real multiple of that unit, and the conventions fix how the numerical value of a quantity is read (a coordinate value alone is a real number, and the unit declaration attaches its dimension). The coordinates of an adapted chart of [[def-cm-affine-time-space]] are read with the time coordinate $t$ in seconds, $[t]=\tau$, and the spatial coordinate components $x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}$ in metres, $[x_{i}]=\ell$; the slice distance $d_{g}$ of [[def-cm-affine-time-space]] between simultaneous events is read in metres.

**(d) Typed quantity conventions.** The following constructions specify the quantities whose dimensions are recorded here, without adopting their dynamics. Fix a positive integer $N$, a nondegenerate open interval $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ with time parameter $t$ in seconds, position curves $x_i:I\to\mathbb R^3$ of class $C^2$ with components in metres, and constant parameters $m_i>0$ in kilograms, for $1\le i\le N$. Derivatives and integrals have the meanings of [[def-vector-valued-derivative-and-integral]]. These are conditional numerical constructions in a fixed spatial coordinate system; whether they represent a particular system is a separate model assumption.

1. **Velocity and acceleration** are the maps $w_i=x_i':I\to\mathbb R^3$ and $a_i=x_i'':I\to\mathbb R^3$, of dimensions $\ell\tau^{-1}$ and $\ell\tau^{-2}$ componentwise.
2. The **mass operator** is the linear map $\mathsf M:(\mathbb R^3)^N\to(\mathbb R^3)^N$, $\mathsf M(z_1,\ldots,z_N)=(m_1z_1,\ldots,m_Nz_N)$, with dimension $\mu$; the **momentum** of label $i$ is $p_i=m_iw_i:I\to\mathbb R^3$, with component dimension $\mu\ell\tau^{-1}$.
3. A **force input** is a specified map $F:I\times O\times\mathbb R^{3N}\to\mathbb R^{3N}$, where $O\subseteq\mathbb R^{3N}$ is open, its arguments are time, positions and velocities, and each output component has dimension $\mu\ell\tau^{-2}$. No regularity or equation equating $F$ with $\mathsf M x''$ is adopted here. A later model must state both if needed.
4. For a specified scalar **potential energy** map $U:I\times O\to\mathbb R$ of dimension $\mu\ell^2\tau^{-2}$ and a tuple $x(t)\in O$, the **kinetic energy** is $T(t)=\tfrac12\sum_{i=1}^N m_i\sum_{j=1}^3(w_i(t))_j^2$, and the **mechanical energy** is $E(t)=T(t)+U(t,x(t))$. Both are real-valued and have dimension $\mu\ell^2\tau^{-2}$; no conservation or applicability to every interaction is asserted.
5. Given a scalar map $L:I\times O\times\mathbb R^{3N}\to\mathbb R$ of the energy dimension and $t_0<t_1$ in $I$, assume $t\mapsto L(t,x(t),w(t))$ is integrable on $[t_0,t_1]$. Its **action on this curve segment** is the real number $S[x;t_0,t_1]=\int_{t_0}^{t_1}L(t,x(t),w(t))\,dt$, with dimension $\mu\ell^2\tau^{-1}$ (the integration convention multiplies the integrand's dimension by duration). No variational principle is imposed.
6. Relative to the chosen spatial origin, define the **angular momentum** $J_i:I\to\mathbb R^3$ by $J_i(t)=x_i(t)\times p_i(t)$, where for $r,s\in\mathbb R^3$ the operation is explicitly $r\times s=(r_2s_3-r_3s_2,r_3s_1-r_1s_3,r_1s_2-r_2s_1)$. Its components have dimension $\mu\ell^2\tau^{-1}$. These quantities depend on the chosen coordinates; dimensions alone assert no transformation or conservation law.
7. A **rotation matrix** here means a real $3\times3$ matrix $R$ satisfying $R^{\mathsf T}R=I_3$ and $\det R=1$; its entries are dimensionless. A radian angle is an arc length divided by its positive radius, hence dimensionless. A generalized coordinate means a component of a specified local coordinate chart on a configuration space; each such component has its own declared dimension, and only quantities of equal dimension are added.

$H_{N,\lambda}:\Gamma_N\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}$, measurable for the
phase Borel sigma-algebra and taking energy values in joules, and the declared
physical reference measure $m_N^{\rm phys}$ of
[[post-csm-counting-and-physical-observables]], choose a prescribed
thermodynamic-temperature control $T>0$ in kelvins and
$\beta=(k_BT)^{-1}$ in J$^{-1}$ using the SI temperature convention of
[[def-td-si-quantities]]. If
$$0<Z_N(\beta,\lambda):=\int_{\Gamma_N}e^{-\beta H_{N,\lambda}}\,dm_N^{\rm phys}<\infty,$$
adopt the canonical state with density
$$\rho_{\beta,\lambda}=Z_N(\beta,\lambda)^{-1}e^{-\beta H_{N,\lambda}}$$
relative to $m_N^{\rm phys}$. Set $e^{-\beta(+\infty)}=0$. Normalizability
is a required condition on the chosen model; bounded-below energy alone does
not imply it. This probability law is an adopted preparation, not a
consequence of deterministic mechanics or evidence of laboratory
equilibration.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice, the exact choice strength required by
[[def-tautological-one-form-on-a-cotangent-bundle]] to construct the smooth
cotangent manifold. Let $d,N\ge1$, let $Q$ be a smooth $d$-manifold, and
choose a countable smooth-chart subcover of its atlas. Such a subcover is
obtained from a countable basis of the second-countable topology by choosing,
for each basis element contained in a chart domain, one such chart domain; this
countable selection is covered by the stated Axiom of Countable Choice. Give
$Q_N:=Q^N$ the product topology and the product smooth structure generated by
the charts
$$\left(U_1\times\cdots\times U_N,\ (q_1,\ldots,q_N)\mapsto(\phi_1(q_1),\ldots,\phi_N(q_N))\right),$$
where each $(U_i,\phi_i)$ belongs to the chosen countable subcover of charts of
$Q$. These images are open in $\mathbb R^{dN}$, and their transition maps are
componentwise smooth, so they form a smooth atlas of dimension $n=dN$; the
finite product of the countable chart family is countable. Its generated
maximal atlas is the product smooth structure in the convention of
[[def-smooth-manifold]]. The induced cotangent charts are indexed by these
base charts and form a countable atlas of $\Gamma_N$. Its
**configuration space** is $Q_N$. Its **phase space** is the cotangent bundle
$$\Gamma_N:=T^*Q_N,$$
whose points are pairs $(q,p)$ with $p\in T_q^*Q_N$. Let
$\pi_N:T^*Q_N\to Q_N$ be the cotangent-bundle projection. The **tautological
one-form** and **canonical symplectic form** are
$$\lambda_{(q,p)}(\xi):=p(d\pi_N\xi),\qquad \omega_N:=-d\lambda.$$
Thus in an induced cotangent chart $(q^1,\ldots,q^n,p_1,\ldots,p_n)$,
$$\lambda=\sum_{j=1}^n p_j\,dq^j,\qquad \omega_N=\sum_{j=1}^n dq^j\wedge dp_j.$$
The cotangent supplier proves $\omega_N$ closed and nondegenerate under the
same Countable Choice premise. On an open phase chart this is exactly the
standard form of [[def-cm-phase-domain-and-standard-symplectic-two-form]];
[[lem-cm-standard-symplectic-form-is-closed-and-nondegenerate]] gives its
closedness, contraction and nondegeneracy coordinate calculations.

Let $\mathcal F_N:=\mathcal B(\Gamma_N)$ be the Borel sigma-algebra generated
by the topology of $\Gamma_N$ ([[def-borel-sigma-algebra]]). The **Liouville
density**, denoted
$$d\Lambda_N:=|\omega_N^{\wedge n}|/n!,$$
is the positive density whose coordinate density in every induced cotangent
chart is $dq^1\cdots dq^n\,dp_1\cdots dp_n$. Define its Borel measure
$\Lambda_N$ explicitly as follows. If $\Gamma_N=\varnothing$,
set $\Lambda_N(\varnothing)=0$. Otherwise choose an at-most-countable induced
cotangent atlas $(V_k,\psi_k)_{k\in J}$ indexed by $J\subseteq\mathbb N$, order
$J$ by the usual order, and set
$$E_k:=V_k\setminus\bigcup_{j\in J,\,j<k}V_j\quad(k\in J).$$
For $A\in\mathcal F_N$, put
$$\Lambda_N(A):=\sum_{k\in J}\lambda_{2n}\bigl(\psi_k(A\cap E_k)\bigr),$$
where $\lambda_{2n}$ is Lebesgue measure on the chart image. Each $E_k$ is
Borel, and each chart map is a homeomorphism, so the terms are defined on
Borel sets. The coordinate transitions preserve $\omega_N$ because
$\omega_N=-d\lambda$ is intrinsic; hence they preserve $\omega_N^n/n!$
and have absolute Jacobian one. For two atlases, the intersections of their
disjoint chart pieces form a countable common Borel refinement. On each
nonempty refinement piece the coordinate transition is a $C^1$ diffeomorphism
with absolute Jacobian one, so the change-of-variables theorem applied to its
indicator [[thm-c-one-change-of-variables-for-nonnegative-lebesgue-measurable-functions]]
gives the same measure from either atlas. Summing over the refinement proves
atlas independence. Countable additivity follows because the chart images of
disjoint Borel sets remain disjoint within each $E_k$ and Lebesgue measure is
countably additive. For the resulting nonnegative array $a_{k\ell}$, both
$\sum_k\sum_\ell a_{k\ell}$ and $\sum_\ell\sum_k a_{k\ell}$ are the
supremum of the same finite subsums of $\{a_{k\ell}\}$, using the
nonnegative extended-sum convention of [[def-measure]]. Hence the sums
reorder and $\Lambda_N$ is a measure with the displayed coordinate density.
Given any finite constant $c_N>0$, define the **labelled reference measure**
$$m_N:=c_N\Lambda_N$$
on $(\Gamma_N,\mathcal F_N)$. It is sigma-finite: $Q_N$ is
countable-atlased as just constructed, so it is covered by countably many
cotangent chart images. Each chart image is open in $\mathbb R^{2n}$ and is
covered by the countable family of bounded open boxes with rational endpoints
whose closures lie in that chart image: every point of an open set lies in one
such box. Each box has finite Euclidean Lebesgue measure, and its chart
preimage therefore has finite $m_N$-measure because the Liouville coordinate
density is the constant $c_N$. The countably many chart-box preimages cover
$\Gamma_N$ and establish sigma-finiteness directly, without a sigma-compactness
supplier.
The constant $c_N$ is mathematical normalization data; this definition assigns
no physical unit to it.

For a partition of the particle labels into species classes of sizes

$Q_N=Q^N$ by permuting factors within each class and on $T^*Q_N$ by the
cotangent lift. In canonical coordinates each lift permutes corresponding
$q$ and $p$ coordinates, so it preserves $\omega_N$, $\Lambda_N$ and $m_N$.
Let $\Pi_N:\Gamma_N\to\Gamma_N/G$ be
the orbit map, equip the orbit set with the quotient sigma-algebra
$$\mathcal F_{\mathrm{quot}}:=\{B\subseteq\Gamma_N/G:\Pi_N^{-1}(B) \text{ is Borel in }\Gamma_N\},$$
and define the **quotient reference measure** by
$$\bar m_N(B):=\frac{1}{\prod_{a=1}^s N_a!}\,m_N(\Pi_N^{-1}(B)).$$
This is a measure because inverse images preserve complements and countable
disjoint unions and $m_N$ is countably additive. The stated invariance makes
it the normalized quotient pushforward. It is a measurable quotient;
no smooth quotient structure at configurations with stabilizers is asserted.
For one species the factor is $1/N!$.

The quotient factor here is mathematical counting data. A physical postulate
determines when labels are operationally indistinguishable and how the
reference scale is interpreted; neither follows from the cotangent geometry.

For a declared classical model with $N_a$ operationally indistinguishable

$$m_N^{\mathrm{phys}}:=\frac{1}{\prod_aN_a!\,a_0^{dN}}\,d\Lambda_N =\frac{1}{\prod_aN_a!\,a_0^{dN}}\,dq\,dp$$
on $\Gamma_N$, where $d\Lambda_N$ is the Liouville density and the last
expression is its coordinate density in canonical charts, with coordinates
read in SI numerical units. The coordinate volume $dq\,dp$ has action
dimension $(\mathrm{J\,s})^{dN}$, so the reference is dimensionless. The

$$\bar m_N^{\mathrm{phys}}(B):=m_N^{\mathrm{phys}}(\Pi_N^{-1}(B))\qquad(B\in\mathcal F_{\mathrm{quot}}).$$
Thus $m_N^{\mathrm{phys}}$ is on the labelled cover $\Gamma_N$, and
$\bar m_N^{\mathrm{phys}}=(\Pi_N)_*m_N^{\mathrm{phys}}$ is on
$\Gamma_N/G$; with $c_N=a_0^{-dN}$, the latter is exactly the normalized
quotient reference of [[def-csm-phase-space-reference]].

Physical observables for indistinguishable particles are measurable

functions $\bar A$ on the quotient with $A=\bar A\circ\Pi_N$. For every such
observable with an integrable expectation, its integral against
$m_N^{\mathrm{phys}}$ equals the quotient integral against
$\bar m_N^{\mathrm{phys}}$. A labelled density represents a physical state on
the quotient only if it is invariant under $G$ almost everywhere with respect
to $m_N^{\mathrm{phys}}$; an invariant representative may then be used. In
particular, an indistinguishable-particle Hamiltonian must be invariant under

when only its Gibbs density is at issue). A label-specific coordinate

permutation-invariant state its marginal law
can instead be interpreted as the law of a uniformly selected particle within
the same species, or of a uniformly selected coordinate of the same type
within that species. Symmetric sums and averages within each species are
quotient observables.

observables.

For a declared classical model with $N_a$ operationally indistinguishable
particles of each species $a$, label those particles by
$\{(a,i):1\le i\le N_a\}$ on the auxiliary labelled cover, and let
$S_{N_a}$ denote the permutation group of that species' finite label set.
The product group $G=\prod_a S_{N_a}$ acts on the labelled phase space
$\Gamma_N=T^*Q_N$ by the cotangent lifts of within-species permutations. Let
$\Pi_N:\Gamma_N\to\Gamma_N/G$ be its measurable orbit map from
[[def-csm-phase-space-reference]]. Choose $a_0>0$ as a fixed primitive
reference parameter with action units J s; [[def-cm01-units]] supplies its
dimension, not its value or the choice of this parameter. Here $d$ is the
number of spatial dimensions and $N=\sum_aN_a$. No numerical value or
identification of $a_0$ with Planck's constant is imposed.

Use the weighted labelled lift
$$m_N^{\mathrm{phys}}:=\frac{1}{\prod_aN_a!\,a_0^{dN}}\,d\Lambda_N =\frac{1}{\prod_aN_a!\,a_0^{dN}}\,dq\,dp$$
on $\Gamma_N$, where $d\Lambda_N$ is the Liouville density and the last
expression is its coordinate density in canonical charts, with coordinates
read in SI numerical units. The coordinate volume $dq\,dp$ has action
dimension $(\mathrm{J\,s})^{dN}$, so the reference is dimensionless. The
physical quotient reference is
$$\bar m_N^{\mathrm{phys}}(B):=m_N^{\mathrm{phys}}(\Pi_N^{-1}(B))\qquad(B\in\mathcal F_{\mathrm{quot}}).$$
Thus $m_N^{\mathrm{phys}}$ is on the labelled cover $\Gamma_N$, and
$\bar m_N^{\mathrm{phys}}=(\Pi_N)_*m_N^{\mathrm{phys}}$ is on
$\Gamma_N/G$; with $c_N=a_0^{-dN}$, the latter is exactly the normalized
quotient reference of [[def-csm-phase-space-reference]].

Physical observables for indistinguishable particles are measurable
$G$-invariant functions $A:\Gamma_N\to\mathbb R$, equivalently measurable
functions $\bar A$ on the quotient with $A=\bar A\circ\Pi_N$. For every such
observable with an integrable expectation, its integral against
$m_N^{\mathrm{phys}}$ equals the quotient integral against
$\bar m_N^{\mathrm{phys}}$. A labelled density represents a physical state on
the quotient only if it is invariant under $G$ almost everywhere with respect
to $m_N^{\mathrm{phys}}$; an invariant representative may then be used. In
particular, an indistinguishable-particle Hamiltonian must be invariant under
these permutations (or agree almost everywhere with its permuted versions
when only its Gibbs density is at issue). A label-specific coordinate
statistic on the lift is not itself a quotient observable. Under a
permutation-invariant state its marginal law
can instead be interpreted as the law of a uniformly selected particle within
the same species, or of a uniformly selected coordinate of the same type
within that species. Symmetric sums and averages within each species are
quotient observables.
Calculations of labelled momentum components in
[[pthm-csm-canonical-momentum-equipartition]] use this symmetric labelled
lift, and their permutation-invariant kinetic sums and averages are physical
observables.

If labels are operationally distinguishable, omit the corresponding
permutation factor and use the labelled phase space directly. The convention
is part of the preparation and reference model; it is not deduced from
Hamiltonian mechanics. Whether a quantity is represented by a gauge-dependent
canonical momentum or by a gauge-invariant mechanical momentum is fixed by the
stated model and gauge convention. No quantum exchange law, actual preparation
mechanism, or empirical indistinguishability test is asserted.

This framework uses the modern International System of Units (SI). The numerical coordinates used elsewhere on this page are divided by their displayed SI units before they are placed in a Euclidean coordinate space.

The model's energy coordinate $U$ and its process-transfer values $Q$ and $W_{\mathrm{on}}$ are scalar energies measured in joules (J). Let $(\Omega,\mathcal F,m)$ be a measure space and let $p,q$ be probability
densities relative to $m$, with $q>0$ almost everywhere on $\{p>0\}$. Define
the relative entropy
$$D(p\Vert q):=\int_{\{p>0\}}p\log(p/q)\,dm,$$
allowing $+\infty$. Then $D(p\Vert q)\ge0$, and equality holds exactly
when $p=q$ almost everywhere. In particular, let $H$ be finite $p$-almost
everywhere, let $\beta>0$, and suppose
$$0<Z=\int e^{-\beta H}dm<\infty,\quad q=Z^{-1}e^{-\beta H},\quad \int p|H|dm<\infty,\quad \int|p\log p|dm<\infty.$$
For $S[p]:=-k\int p\log p\,dm$ and $F:=-\beta^{-1}\log Z$, with $k>0$
and $\beta kT=1$, one has
$$D(p\Vert q)=\beta\bigl(\langle H\rangle_p-F-TS[p]\bigr)\ge0.$$
Thus the Gibbs density minimizes this specified free-energy functional
among the stated densities; this mathematical inequality does not derive a
physical preparation.

derivations.claim: For $r$ particles in position volume $W$, separate the $r$ position integrals and use [F1] in all $dr$ momentum coordinates. For one coordinate put $a=\beta/(2m)$; integrating $\frac{d}{dp}(pe^{-ap^2})=e^{-ap^2}-2ap^2e^{-ap^2}$ over $\mathbb R$ gives $\langle p^2\rangle=m/\beta$, as the boundary term vanishes by Gaussian decay. Thus the mean kinetic energy is $dr/(2\beta)$. The position law factorizes into $r$ uniform position laws. With $\lambda_T=a_0\sqrt{\beta/(2\pi m)}$, the partition function is $$Z_r(W)=\frac{W^r}{r!a_0^{dr}}\left(\frac{2\pi m}{\beta}\right)^{dr/2} =\frac{(W/\lambda_T^d)^r}{r!}.$$ For equal total particle count $2N$ before and after, the $\beta U$ terms in [F2] cancel, so the entropy change is $k_B$ times the logarithm of the partition-function ratio.

Initially the ratio is $Z_{2N}(2V)/Z_N(V)^2$ $=4^N(N!)^2/(2N)!$; for two fixed distinguishable species it is $[Z_N(2V)/Z_N(V)]^2=4^N$. The first ratio exceeds one because $(2N)!/(N!)^2=\binom{2N}{N}<\sum_{j=0}^{2N}\binom{2N}{j}=4^N$. Under the final positional law, the $2N$ particles independently fall in either half with probability $1/2$, so the central binomial probability is $\binom{2N}{N}/4^N$, the reciprocal of the identical-particle ratio.

For each integer $n\ge1$, monotonicity of $\log x$ on unit intervals gives $$n\log n-n+1\le\log(n!)\le n\log n-n+1+\log n.$$ Indeed the lower bound integrates $\log x\le\log j$ on $[j-1,j]$ for $j=2,\ldots,n$, and the upper bound integrates $\log x\ge\log j$ on $[j,j+1]$ for $j=1,\ldots,n-1$, then adds $\log n$. Substitution for $n=N$ and $n=2N$ cancels the terms linear in $N$ in $N\log4+2\log(N!)-\log((2N)!)$, leaving a quantity bounded in absolute value by a constant multiple of $\log(N+1)$. Therefore $\Delta S_{\mathrm{identical}}/N\to0$ as $N\to\infty$.

**(a) Dimensions.** Write $\ell$, $\tau$, $\mu$ for the three independent *dimension symbols* of length, duration and mass. A **dimension** is an element of the free abelian group generated by $\ell,\tau,\mu$, that is, a triple $(a,b,c)\in\mathbb Z^3$ written $\ell^{a}\tau^{b}\mu^{c}$; **products and inverses** of dimensions are componentwise addition and negation, so that $\ell^{a}\tau^{b}\mu^{c}\cdot\ell^{a'}\tau^{b'}\mu^{c'}=\ell^{a+a'}\tau^{b+b'}\mu^{c+c'}$ and $(\ell^{a}\tau^{b}\mu^{c})^{-1}=\ell^{-a}\tau^{-b}\mu^{-c}$. **(b) The dimension map.** The conventions assign to the quantities of the framework a **dimension** $[X]$, subject to the rules

$$[XY]=[X][Y],\qquad [X/Y]=[X][Y]^{-1},\qquad \left[\frac{dX}{du}\right]=[X][u]^{-1},$$

and to the requirement that a sum $X+Y$ is meaningful only when $[X]=[Y]$, in which case $[X+Y]=[X]$. The third rule applies to a differentiable dependence of a quantity $X$ on a quantity $u$ and covers iterated differentiation, so that $[d^{2}X/du^{2}]=[X][u]^{-2}$. The assignment is part of the conventions: the rules above are consistency requirements on it, not physical laws and not theorems.

A quantity of dimension $\ell^{a}\tau^{b}\mu^{c}$ is expressed in the unit $\mathrm m^{a}\,\mathrm s^{b}\,\mathrm{kg}^{c}$: its value is a real multiple of that unit, and the conventions fix how the numerical value of a quantity is read (a coordinate value alone is a real number, and the unit declaration attaches its dimension). The coordinates of an adapted chart of [[def-cm-affine-time-space]] are read with the time coordinate $t$ in seconds, $[t]=\tau$, and the spatial coordinate components $x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}$ in metres, $[x_{i}]=\ell$; the slice distance $d_{g}$ of [[def-cm-affine-time-space]] between simultaneous events is read in metres.

**(d) Typed quantity conventions.** The following constructions specify the quantities whose dimensions are recorded here, without adopting their dynamics. Fix a positive integer $N$, a nondegenerate open interval $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ with time parameter $t$ in seconds, position curves $x_i:I\to\mathbb R^3$ of class $C^2$ with components in metres, and constant parameters $m_i>0$ in kilograms, for $1\le i\le N$. Derivatives and integrals have the meanings of [[def-vector-valued-derivative-and-integral]]. These are conditional numerical constructions in a fixed spatial coordinate system; whether they represent a particular system is a separate model assumption.

1. **Velocity and acceleration** are the maps $w_i=x_i':I\to\mathbb R^3$ and $a_i=x_i'':I\to\mathbb R^3$, of dimensions $\ell\tau^{-1}$ and $\ell\tau^{-2}$ componentwise.
2. The **mass operator** is the linear map $\mathsf M:(\mathbb R^3)^N\to(\mathbb R^3)^N$, $\mathsf M(z_1,\ldots,z_N)=(m_1z_1,\ldots,m_Nz_N)$, with dimension $\mu$; the **momentum** of label $i$ is $p_i=m_iw_i:I\to\mathbb R^3$, with component dimension $\mu\ell\tau^{-1}$.

4. For a specified scalar **potential energy** map $U:I\times O\to\mathbb R$ of dimension $\mu\ell^2\tau^{-2}$ and a tuple $x(t)\in O$, the **kinetic energy** is $T(t)=\tfrac12\sum_{i=1}^N m_i\sum_{j=1}^3(w_i(t))_j^2$, and the **mechanical energy** is $E(t)=T(t)+U(t,x(t))$. A generalized coordinate means a component of a specified local coordinate chart on a configuration space; each such component has its own declared dimension, and only quantities of equal dimension are added.

derivations.claim: Integrating the momentum factors gives [F1]; integrating the unit shape coordinates gives one, while the configuration scaling contributes $V^N$. Hence $$\Delta_N=\frac{1}{N!V_0a_0^n}\left(\frac{2\pi m}{\beta}\right)^{n/2} \int_0^\infty V^Ne^{-sV}dV,\qquad s=\beta P_{\rm ext}>0.$$ Let $I_j(s)=\int_0^\infty V^je^{-sV}dV$. Direct integration gives $I_0=1/s$; integration by parts, with $V^je^{-sV}\to0$ at infinity and vanishing lower boundary for $j\ge1$, gives $I_j=jI_{j-1}/s$. Thus $I_j=j!/s^{j+1}$, and $I_N=N!/s^{N+1}$ cancels the $N!$ in the reference; the displayed finite positive normalizer follows.

The normalized volume density is $V^Ne^{-sV}/I_N(s)$. Applying the same integral formula to $I_{N+1}$ and $I_{N+2}$ gives $\langle V\rangle=(N+1)/s$ and $\langle V^2\rangle=(N+1)(N+2)/s^2$. Subtracting the square of the mean gives $\operatorname{Var}(V)=(N+1)/s^2$. Since $s=\beta P_{\rm ext}$, these are the claimed volume moments.

For each fixed $V$, [F1] and Gaussian integration by parts give $\langle K\mid V\rangle=n/(2\beta)$. The volume density has exponential tail $e^{-sV}$ and all polynomial moments from step 1.1, so the local envelopes in [F2] hold on compact positive $\beta,P_{\rm ext}$ sets. Consequently $P_{\rm ext}\langle V\rangle=(N+1)/\beta$, and adding the kinetic mean gives $\langle K+P_{\rm ext}V\rangle=(n/2+N+1)/\beta$.
